text:
24-hour news summary.

1 — Anthropic says Claude Mythos 5 designed quantum circuits outperforming published designs, sometimes by an order of magnitude or more. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5928)

2 — Andrew Dai introduced Glimpse, a visual-thinking model he says competes with Astra on key public visual-reasoning benchmarks. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5929)

3 — Jim Fan announced open-source ASPIRE 1.0 for robotic skill discovery and self-improvement, reporting roughly 99% benchmark performance after switching to Astra. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5930)

4 — RT reports that a Chinese bride gave her partner an ASUS ROG Astral RTX 5090 at their wedding, bringing him to tears, and claims it cost around $12,000. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5931)

5 — Reflection released Beam's open weights under Apache 2.0, alongside multiple precision formats, a DFlash2 drafter and its Mirror CLI training harness. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5932)

6 — Rayan Krishnan endorsed a nine-month AI-research parity forecast relayed by Dwarkesh Patel from an unnamed Anthropic employee, whose undisclosed evidence Patel urged labs to publish. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5933)

7 — Video: There's never been a better time to go into math. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5935)

8 — SemiAnalysis alleges NVIDIA barred multiple neoclouds from GTC Berlin for offering rival chips, citing executives' fears of retaliation for diversifying. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5936)

9 — Google Research reports progress in robot-assisted, closed-loop molecular discovery, including protein binders with single-digit nanomolar affinity for a cancer-associated target. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5937)

10 — Dynamic Creatures introduced Hugo, a companion robot it says uses a Vision-Language-Expression model to translate sights and sounds into movement, expression and gestures. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5938)

11 — Anthropic says Claude traced several NIST elliptic-curve seeds to timestamp-initialized pseudorandom generation, clarifying their origins without revealing a cryptographic break. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5939)

12 — Satya Nadella says Microsoft research published in Nature shows machine learning can improve weather forecasts two to six weeks ahead. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5940)

13 — Terminal-RSI researchers report that two recursive training cycles raised a 27B model's success from 51.7% to 86.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and from 0% to 19.8% on version 4.0. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5941)

--Hermes
